newsitem.title: USA: Cali to buy Mack, Patriot assets in $1.2 billion deal.
newsitem.headline: Cali to buy Mack, Patriot assets in $1.2 billion deal.

text.p: Cali Realty Corp. said on Thursday it will buy the office real estate portfolios of Mack Co. and Patriot American Office Group for $1.2 billion, creating one of the largest real estate investment trusts in the country.
The transaction, which is expected to close by year-end, will also make Cali the dominant player in the New Jersey real estate market.

The company, to be renamed Mack-Cali Realty Corp., will have a market capitalization of $3.3 billion. It will own 8 percent, or about 11 million square feet, of all office space in central and northern New Jersey.
Under the deal, Cali will add 55 office properties totaling about 9.5 million square feet in the Northeast and Southwest to its portfolio, for a combined portfolio of 185 properties in 10 states.

New Jersey-based Mack Co. owns 17 million square feet of space in and around New Jersey, about 35 percent of which is offices, as well as other property in Arizona. Patriot American, based in Dallas, owns 17 office buildings in Dallas, Houston, San Antonio and Amarillo. Both companies are privately held.

The deal calls for Mack Co. to contribute its 5.9 million square-foot class A office portfolio and related operations. Patriot American Office Group will contribute its 3.6 million square-foot portfolio and related operations.
Cali President and Chief Executive Thomas Rizk will remain chief executive of Mack-Cali Realty Corp.
"This merger represents an historic opportunity for Cali and its shareholders," Rizk said in a statement.
"It truly solidifies our position as the dominant super-regional REIT in the Northeast, plus it provides us with new strategic beachheads in the Southwest for future growth opportunities," he said.

William Mack will serve as a director and chairman of the executive committee and Mitchell Hersh, partner and chief operating officer of the Mack Co., will serve as president and chief operating officer of Mack-Cali.
The terms of the agreement call for Cali to pay $476 million in cash and assume $302 million of mortgage debt.

Cali also will issue 3.9 million common operating units in Cali Realty, L.P. and issue $250 million of preferred operating units in Cali Realty, L.P., paying a 6.75 percent distribution and convertible into 7.2 million common operating units.
In addition, Cali will issue warrants to purchase two million shares of its stock at $37.80 apiece.
Cali's stock gained $1.875 to $37.625 on the New York Stock Exchange.
